(target_width, target _ height)) imagel_resized = # Blend the images using OpenCV's addition method blended_image cv2.add (imagel_resized, image2_rgb) put . imshow (blended_image) put. titte( 'Blended Image (cv2.add) ptt . axis(' off') put . show() Description : FAST NUCES - This code Uses OpenCV to read two separate images and blend them together. Because Matplotlib expects colors in RGB format, both images are first converted from OpenCV's default BGR format. In order to mathematically combine two images, they must have the exact same pixel dimensions. The code retrieves the height and width of the second image and Uses cv2.resize() to force the first image to match those exact dimensions. Once the sizes match, the images are combined using cv2.add(). This function performs matrix addition, adding the intensity values of corresponding pixels together. A key feature of OpenCV's add() function is that it uses saturation arithmetic—meaning if the sum of two pixel values exceeds the maximum limit of 255, it caps the result at exactly 255 (pure white) rather than rotting over. Because values are being added together, the resulting blended image witt generally took much brighter than either originat image. Finally, the combined image is displayed intine using Matplotlib.
